offer_letter.markdown:
# Offer of employment — Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy

## 1. Our offer to you

Dear {{employee.full_name}}, we are glad to offer you the job of Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy at Absa Group. This is a permanent job. You will start on 1 December 2026. Your place of work is Johannesburg, head office.

## 2. What you will do

You will give highly specialised legal advice and support to the area you support. You will act as a senior legal subject-matter expert on data privacy and data protection law, regulatory matters and financial crime. You will review Privacy Impact Assessments, compliance assessments, new products, projects, technologies, processes and proposed data-use arrangements. You will draft, review and negotiate data protection provisions, data processing and data sharing agreements, consent wording, privacy notices and other privacy documents. You will manage external counsel, represent the Bank at internal committees and industry forums, and give legal training to internal clients. We may also ask you to do other reasonable duties that fit the position.

## 3. Pay, hours and leave

Your basic salary is R18,000.00 per month. We pay on the 25th of each month by EFT. We will deduct PAYE and UIF of 1%. You will work 40 hours per week, 8 hours a day over 5 days, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00, with a meal break of 60 minutes. You get 15 working days of paid annual leave each 12-month cycle, 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle, 3 days' family responsibility leave a year, 4 months' maternity leave and 10 days' parental leave.

## 4. Probation and notice

Your first 3 months are a probation period. During this time we will assess your work and give you fair guidance and support. Notice to end the job is one week if you have worked six months or less, two weeks if you have worked more than six months but not more than one year, and four weeks after one year.

## 5. Next steps

This offer is open until 30 November 2026. Please send us your ID and your qualifications. If you have questions, write to hr@example.co.za.

## 6. Acceptance

I accept this offer: {{employee.full_name}}, signed on {{date_signed}}.

# Contract of employment — Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy

## 1. Parties

This contract of employment is entered into between Absa Group, of 1 Main Road, Johannesburg (the Employer), and {{employee.full_name}}, identity number {{employee.id_number}}, of {{employee.address}} (the Employee).

## 2. Position and duties

The Employer appoints the Employee as Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy. The Employee's duties include: To provide highly specialised legal advice and support to the dedicated area of support.; Act as a senior legal subject-matter expert on data privacy and data protection law, regulatory and financial crime.; Review and legally assess Privacy Impact Assessments, compliance assessments, new products, projects, technologies, processes and proposed data-use arrangements.; Provide independent legal advice on novel and complex data use, data sharing, disclosure, retention, cross-border transfer and related privacy matters across the Bank, the Group and ARO.; Draft, review and negotiate data protection provisions, data processing and data sharing agreements, consent wording, privacy notices, forms, customer communications and other privacy-related documentation.; Build strong client relationships and engage confidently with stakeholders at different levels of seniority, managing complex or conflicting expectations professionally and effectively.; Independently plan, prioritise and manage a broad portfolio of matters from instruction through to completion, taking ownership and providing clear legal advice, direction and follow-up.; Contribute to the development and achievement of team objectives and strategy, while providing high-quality support to business and Legal stakeholders.; Represent the Bank independently as a subject-matter expert at internal committees, governance forums, industry engagements and professional bodies, and supervise others where appropriate.; Demonstrate strong analytical skills and solve complex problems creatively and effectively; Drive good cost-control behaviour, particularly in relation to external legal spend, and consistently deliver against a broad range of competing priorities and deadlines.; Manage external counsel; Add value in commercial and technical discussions, translate complex privacy requirements into practical business advice, and provide relevant legal training to internal clients.; Strengthen Legal’s contribution to the effective identification, management and mitigation of legal risk across the business.; Promote awareness of, and support adherence to, applicable legal policies and control requirements.; Build effective partnerships with Risk, Compliance and other key control functions to support coordinated and effective risk management.; Collaborate proactively across teams and geographies within Legal, contributing to the development and achievement of team objectives and helping to break down silos.; Share knowledge and expertise openly, provide objective and constructive feedback, and contribute to the planning and delivery of Legal Function knowledge sessions.; Act as a trusted legal advisor to business and infrastructure functions, providing clear, practical advice on relevant legal and market developments and their business impact.; Proactively monitor domestic and international privacy and regulatory developments, assess their legal and practical impact on the Bank, the Group and ARO, and communicate implications and recommended actions clearly and timeously.; Represent the Bank as a subject-matter expert at internal committees and industry forums, contributing to industry initiatives and maintaining a strong external professional network.. The Employer may reasonably require the Employee to perform other duties consistent with the position.

## 3. Commencement

Employment commences on 1 December 2026 on a permanent basis.

## 4. Probation

The first 3 month(s) of employment are a probationary period during which the Employer will assess the Employee's performance against the requirements of the position and give reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. Confirmation, extension or termination at the end of probation will follow a fair procedure.

## 5. Place of work

The Employee's place of work is Johannesburg, head office.

## 6. Hours of work

The Employee's ordinary hours of work are 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day over 5 days per week (Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00). A meal interval of 60 minutes is taken after no more than five hours of continuous work. The Employee is entitled to a daily rest period of at least 12 consecutive hours and a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours.

## 7. Remuneration

The Employee will be paid R18,000.00 per month (basic salary), equivalent to R103.85 per ordinary hour, payable monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments are payable. No payments in kind are made.

## 8. Overtime

Overtime is worked only by agreement and may not exceed ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the Employee's ordinary hourly wage, or, by agreement, compensated with paid time off. Work on a Sunday is paid at double the ordinary wage (or one and a half times if the Employee ordinarily works on Sundays), and work on a public holiday at double the ordinary wage.

## 9. Deductions

The following deductions will be made from the Employee's remuneration: PAYE; UIF 1%. No other deduction will be made without the Employee's written agreement in respect of a specific debt, or as required by law, a court order or an arbitration award.

## 10. Leave

The Employee is entitled to 15 working days of paid annual leave per annual leave cycle of 12 months, to be taken at a time agreed with the Employer and not later than six months after the end of the cycle. Sick leave: 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle (during the first six months, one day for every 26 days worked); a medical certificate may be required for absences of more than two consecutive days or on more than two occasions in eight weeks. Maternity leave: at least 4 consecutive months. Parental leave: 10 consecutive days. Adoption and commissioning parental leave as provided in the Act. Family responsibility leave: 3 days' paid leave per year once employed for longer than four months and for at least four days a week.

## 11. Termination and notice

Either party may terminate this contract on written notice of one week if the employee has been employed for six months or less; two weeks if employed for more than six months but not more than one year; four weeks if employed for more than one year. Notice may not be given during any period of leave. Nothing in this clause prevents the Employer from terminating employment summarily for a fair reason following a fair procedure, or the parties from agreeing to waive notice.

## 12. Bargaining council or sectoral determination

No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to the Employer's business.

## 13. Confidentiality

The Employee will not, during or after employment, disclose or use any confidential information of the Employer, its clients or suppliers, except as required to perform the Employee's duties or by law.

## 14. Other documents

No other documents form part of this contract.

## 15. General

This contract records the whole agreement between the parties on its subject; any amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties. Where any term is less favourable to the Employee than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the more favourable provision applies. The Employer will keep these particulars for three years after termination and will explain them to the Employee on request.

## 16. Signatures

For the Employer: {{employer.signatory}}  ____________________

The Employee: {{employee.full_name}}  ____________________

plain_language.explanation: This says who the agreement is between. The employer is Absa Group, at 1 Main Road, Johannesburg. You are the employee, named with your identity number and your address.

You are appointed as Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy. The clause lists your duties, which include specialised legal advice, data privacy and data protection expertise, reviewing Privacy Impact Assessments and new products, drafting and negotiating data agreements and privacy notices, managing external counsel, controlling external legal spend, training internal clients, monitoring privacy and regulatory developments, and representing the Bank at committees and industry forums. The employer may also ask you to do other duties that reasonably fit this position.
Your job starts on 1 December 2026. The job is permanent, so it has no set end date.

Your first 3 months are a probation period. During this time the employer will check your work against what the job needs, and give you fair evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling if you need it. At the end of probation the employer may confirm you, extend probation, or end your employment, and must follow a fair procedure.
You will work at Johannesburg, head office. That is your place of work under this contract.

You work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, over 5 days, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You get a 60-minute meal break after no more than five hours of continuous work. You also get at least 12 hours of rest in a row each day and at least 36 hours of rest in a row each week.
You are paid R18,000.00 per month as basic salary, which works out to R103.85 per ordinary hour. Payment is made monthly on the 25th by EFT. There are no other cash payments and no payments in kind.

You only work overtime if you agree, and it cannot be more than ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times your ordinary hourly wage, or you can agree to take paid time off instead. Sunday work is paid at double your ordinary wage, or one and a half times if you normally work Sundays, and public holiday work is paid at double.
The employer will take PAYE and UIF of 1% off your pay. No other deduction may be made unless you agree in writing for a specific debt, or the law, a court order or an arbitration award requires it.

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave for each 12-month leave cycle, taken at a time agreed with the employer and no later than six months after the cycle ends. You get 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle, but in your first six months you get one day for every 26 days worked; a medical certificate may be asked for if you are off more than two days in a row, or more than twice in eight weeks. You also get at least 4 consecutive months' maternity leave, 10 consecutive days' parental leave, adoption and commissioning parental leave as set out in the Act, and 3 days' paid family responsibility leave a year once you have worked longer than four months and work at least four days a week.

You or the employer can end the contract with written notice: one week if you have been employed six months or less, two weeks if more than six months but not more than one year, and four weeks if more than one year. Notice cannot be given while you are on leave. The employer may still dismiss you immediately for a fair reason after a fair procedure, and both sides may agree to skip notice.
No bargaining council agreement applies to the employer's business. No sectoral determination applies either.

You may not share or use confidential information of the employer, its clients or its suppliers. This applies while you work there and after you leave. The only exceptions are when you need it to do your job or when the law requires it.
No other documents form part of this contract. Only the terms written in this contract apply.

This contract is the full agreement on what it covers, and any change must be written down and signed by both of you. If a term here is worse for you than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the better provision applies instead. The employer must keep these particulars for three years after your employment ends and must explain them to you if you ask.
This is the signature block. The employer's signatory signs for Absa Group, and you sign as the employee. It also records the place and the date of signing.
